title.narrative: Uplands Irrigation and Water Resources Management Sector Project

description.narrative:
The proposed Uplands Irrigation and Water Resources Management Sector Project will help the Government of Cambodia increase agricultural production by rehabilitating, modernizing, and climate-proofing selected irrigation systems in Kampong Thom and Battambang provinces. Subprojects will be undertaken to (i) enhance the efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems, and (ii) improve water resource management by building the capacity of government agencies and of farmer water user communities (FWUCs) so that they can operate and manage the irrigation systems better. The project will contribute to achieving targets defined in the government's strategy. The strategy aims to develop and expand the country's irrigated land and manage its water resources more effectively by improving existing irrigation systems, making water user communities more efficient, and reducing the vulnerability of the Cambodia's people to disasters caused by natural hazards. The project is included in the Asian Development Bank (ADB) country operations business plan for Cambodia for 2015-2017.
The project impact will be inclusive economic growth through agriculture and irrigation, in line with phase 3 of the government's Rectangular Strategy on Growth, Employment, Equity, and Efficiency for 2014-2018. The outcome will be water and agriculture productivity enhanced in the project area. The project will deliver two outputs: (i) Output 1: Enhanced efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems in the project area; and (ii) Output 2: Improved water resource management.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems in the project area enhanced Indicator: 1c. Drainage facilities for 1,800 ha improved (2015 baseline: 0 ha) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Drainage facilities improved from 0 ha to 1,780 ha, of which, Taing Krasaing (TK) - 600 ha; O Kra Nhak (OKN) - 0 ha; and Prek Chik (PC) - 1,180 ha Data Source: 1c. PPMS

Output: 1. Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems in the project area enhanced Indicator: 1d. 2,000 ha land leveled by laser leveling (2015 baseline: 0 ha) Achievement: 200 Progress/Status: The laser land leveling contract was completed in September 2020 and accomplished 99.9 ha in TK and 100.7 ha in PC for a total of 200.6 ha. Data Source: 1d-f. QPRs, PPMS

Output: 1. Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems in the project area enhanced Indicator: 1e. 21,000 ha land improved through irrigation, drainage, and/or flood protection Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 21,026 ha of land have been improved (TK- 6,964 ha; OKN- 1,762 ha; PC- 11,500 ha, and OTC: 1,800). Data Source: QPRs of the executing agency, PPMS, LRM reports

Output: 1. Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems in the project area enhanced Indicator: 1f. 25% of unskilled laborers in civil works are women Achievement: 25.36 Progress/Status: 257,292 person-days of unskilled laborers have been recruited, including 67,301 person-days of women (26.2%). Data Source: QPRs of the executing agency, PPMS, LRM reports

Output: 2. Water resource management improved Indicator: 2b. 30% of FWUC members are women (2015 baseline: 0) Achievement: 53 Progress/Status: Total membership in FWUCs is 5,101 HHs consisting of 18,220 persons including 8,678 women or 48% of total. Member of women in three FWUCS: • TK FWUC: 1,009 HHs consisting of 3,355 persons including 1,631 women (49%). • OKN FWUC: 547 HHs consisting of 1,001 persons including 483 women (48%). • PC FWUC: 3,545 HHs consisting of 13,864 persons including 6,564 women (47%).
Data Source: 2e. Ministry of Economy and Finance budget documents, QPRs, LRM reports

Output: 2. Water resource management improved Indicator: 2c. 30% of FWUC management committee members are women (2015 baseline: 0) Achievement: 28 Progress/Status: FWUC management committees have 135 members including 48 women (36%).
Membership of women in each FWUC management committee: • TK FWUC: 36 members including 13 women (36%). • OKN FWUC:38 members including 14 women (37%). • PC FWUC (including OTC FWUG): 61 members including 21 women (34%). Data Source: 2f. QPRs, LRM reports, PPMS

Output: 2. Water resource management improved Indicator: 2f. Eight hydrometeorological stations installed in the watersheds (2015 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 15 automatic weather stations (AWSs) and 15 automatic hydro-meteorological stations (AHSs) were installed in 2017. The data collected by the stations and automatically sent to the data server in every 15 minutes in MOWRAM. This data provides real time monitoring of water levels and rainfall and can be quickly shared with the public via mobile networks and the internet. Data Source: QPRs, LRM reports, PPMS

Output: 2. Water resource management improved Indicator: By 2021: 2a. Three FWUCs formed and trained (2015 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Three farmer water users communities (FWUCs) and one FWUG have been formed [Taing Krasaing (TK)- 1; Okra Nhak (OKN)-1; and Prek Chik (PC)- 1]. The OTC FWUC has been integrated into PC FWUC. Training has been completed for all three FWUCs and one FWUG. Data Source: 2a-d. QPRs, LRM reports

Output: 1. Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems in the project area enhanced Indicator: By 2021: 1a. Irrigation infrastructure improved, modernized and climate-proofed. Dry- and wet-season cultivated area increased to 29,500 ha (2015 baseline: 13,500 ha) Achievement: 10114 Progress/Status: The project is providing irrigation water to at least 31,140 ha, of which 21,026 ha for wet season and 10,1147 ha for dry season, equivalent to 106% of the target of 29,500 ha. Data Source: 1a. QPRs of the executing agency, PPMS, LRM reports

Output: 1. Efficiency and climate resilience of irrigation systems in the project area enhanced Indicator: 1b. Irrigation efficiency of three irrigation systems increased by 100% (2015 baseline: 20% efficiency) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Assessment could only be undertaken during the operation of the irrigation systems equipped with canal flow measuring system.
Efficiency of irrigation service delivery, as indicated by irrigated area in the dry season increased more than 100% from 1,125 ha without the project to 2,444 ha in 2020 and 4,147 ha in 2021.
Data Source: 1b. PPMS

Output: 2. Water resource management improved Indicator: 2d. Annual O&M plan prepared during design of each irrigation system Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Annual O&M plan has been prepared for each scheme of which annual O&M plan for TK irrigation scheme has been submitted in Sep. 2020, OKN submitted in December 2020, and PC-OTC submitted in April 2021.The tripartite agreement for Taing Krasang irrigation system have been signed and and is being implemented. Data Source: QPRs, LRM reports, PPMS Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 2. Water resource management improved Indicator: 2e. O&M funds allocated by the government for main canals and reservoirs Achievement: N Progress/Status: PMU/MOWRAM has been working on this with MEF. MOWRAM Irrigation Department submitted the 2021 and 2022 O&M proposal for the three systems. MEF has yet to approve the proposal. Data Source: QPRs, LRM reports, PPMS Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: N
Water and agriculture productivity enhanced in the project area

By 2022: Average annual crop production increased to 4.25 ton per ha (2015 baseline: 1.65 tons per ha) Achievement: 4.42 Progress/Status: Focus Group Discussion conducted by the EA in July 2021 showed average yield of 4.42 t/ha in the three irrigation systems. The achievement on the indicator showed that the outcome is likely to be achieved. Project full development is still about 2-3 years ahead. Data Source: PPMS
